memory_candidates.content: A jq-defs-as-heredoc shared library (the `read -r -d '' VAR <<'EOF' ... EOF` idiom used by lib/file-scope-overlap.sh and similar single-source-of-truth jq libraries) returns exit 1 when sourced, because `read -d ''` reports non-zero on reaching the heredoc's EOF without ever seeing a literal NUL delimiter -- even though the variable assignment itself succeeded in full. Under a caller's `set -e` this aborts sourcing immediately and silently (the library's own content is correct; only the source-time exit status is wrong). Fix: append `|| true` directly to the `read` invocation inside the library itself, so a plain `source`/`.` is always safe regardless of the caller's shell options, rather than requiring every consumer to wrap the source call in its own `if ! ...; then` guard.

When two independently-written scripts must agree on one computed bound (e.g. an allocator and its validator both deciding what counts as 'in use'), extracting the shared jq logic into a single library that exports its `def` source as a bash string (spliced as an adjacent string literal immediately before each caller's own jq program, e.g. `"$SHARED_DEFS"'...rest of program...'`) removes the duplication entirely rather than just keeping two expressions aligned by a header comment. This is the same shape lib/file-scope-overlap.sh already uses for FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS; following an existing precedent exactly (including its documented contract: no shell options set, never calls exit, one deliberate export) made the new library predictable to review and consume.

A 'membership' bound (reject only if the candidate value is already in use) is strictly more precise than a 'maximum' bound (reject unless the candidate exceeds the largest value ever seen) for a number allocator recovering from sparse historical gaps -- the maximum bound forces the counter arbitrarily high past a handful of isolated outliers, even when the dense range between the current issue point and those outliers is entirely free. Pairing the membership check with a derived-value design (the issued number is always computed fresh from the in-use set, and the stored counter becomes a regenerated CACHE rather than an authority) makes the counter's own correctness unconditional rather than dependent on being kept monotonically repaired by every caller.
